Independent approved descriptors and owned exact artifact snapshots precede one Factory.Load. Factory remains trusted and must attest actual loaded evaluator/tool/dependencies; no universal loader or isolation is supplied.

Closed local root rules fix recipient, role-bound signing key, tool, exact canonical arguments and lifetime. A trusted application selects appropriate rules; hashes do not prove natural-language equivalence.
Bounded confined regular files are checked against each declared hash. Trusted administration must protect and serialize intermediate paths; this is not concurrent hostile-filesystem isolation.
The bounded opened artifact is checked as regular before reading. Operating-system support is reviewed separately.

Original capture and exact files are rechecked before and after the trusted loaded-instance callback. Active integrity failure retires this operation; Check must attest real loaded code, not echo commitments.
Requires exact canonical object bytes for fixed arguments and root intent input.
A context-aware shared gate serializes checks and final execution with retirement. Local serialization is not distributed epoch management.
Returns owned approved descriptors only for the fixed issuer and request after current capture/artifact/instance checks. Wire commitments cannot install mappings.
Exact issuer/tool/arguments are locally evaluated before current integrity checks. This callback is a policy snapshot, not one-use approval, reservation or dispatch.

Manually reviewed closed root intent fields, identity, commitments, nonce and lifetime match fixed administration. Parent intents are refused; core retains current authority/time, opaque approval and durable issuance fencing.
Fixed manifest/tool identity is checked before capture/artifact/same-instance remeasurement. Actual attestation remains a deployment provider duty.
The private loaded wrapper delegates measurement to the same Operation used by native host Binding.

Only the fixed instance receives a copy of exact arguments after fresh checks under the shared gate. Binding.Tool is a trusted capability; exposing it as unsigned model dispatch is outside the protected path.
Returns a private wrapper tied to this Operation for trusted native host configuration. Constructing it does not wrap ordinary Agent, Tool Registry, A2A or gRPC routes.

Refuses new callbacks before waiting for accepted effect cleanup and closing artifact custody. Timeout retains ownership/refusal; administration still owns factory lifetime, durable epochs and distributed retirement.
Copies exact owned artifact bytes for a protected Factory. This copy is not an execution or signing token.
Returns owned canonical policy descriptor bytes, not policy authority.
Returns owned canonical component manifest bytes, not loaded-code attestation.
Linux/macOS use confined no-follow nonblocking final opens; final descriptor inspection is separate. Intermediate mutations still require trusted serialized administration.
Other operating systems refuse artifact opening. Parsing mutually exclusive source files does not prove runtime platform selection.
Cancellation is checked around the shared gate; provider bounds and cancellation remain trusted obligations.
Absent or typed-nil measurement and instance limits outside 1..1024 are refused; protected configuration must select the provider.

Reviewed control flow covers configuration and named image in component/evaluator descriptors, mandatory measurement before fixed compiled tool construction and bounded private ownership. No snapshot code is loaded. Measurement must prove protected pre-load verification and retained immutable runtime identity; the call is not attestation.
Selects component manifest paths from owned snapshot artifacts; exact bytes are verified by Factory.Load.
Closed five-field configuration fixes version, tool, image path, sorted unique arithmetic operations and finite positive operand bound. Image path is descriptor data, not a dynamic load request.
Actual runtime measurement is mandatory; retirement is rechecked after the callback and failed checks retire the private instance. No concrete measurement provider is supplied here.
Exact policy/component commitments and calculator identity precede runtime measurement under the instance gate; panics refuse and retire.

Canonical closed operation/a/b arguments and configured finite bounds precede repeated measurement and the same private tool callback; output is canonicalized. This trusted Instance capability must stay behind guardbinding and native admission, not a model-facing unsigned dispatcher.

Retirement refuses new work and waits for accepted bounded callbacks before clearing tool/snapshot ownership. Cancelled cleanup retains ownership for retry; blocked providers require their own bounds.

Existing compiled arithmetic constructor is used by the opt-in private adapter. Direct use remains unmediated; division by zero is a domain-error result and completed execution does not imply domain success.
Nil or cancelled contexts refuse operations. Context checks are local bounds, not host attestation.
Context-aware shared gate serializes appraisal and cleanup. Cancellation restores acquired gate ownership; this is not cross-process effect mediation.
Native Linux amd64/arm64 restriction and owned byte approval precede platform start; success retains one private backend. Creating it does not select a deployed host.
Explicit bounded image input is copied and compared with an independently approved digest before static executable profile validation. Caller-supplied baseline needs protected administration.

Bounded native ELF executable with file-backed entry, no interpreter/dynamic segment, executable stack or writable executable load; Go metadata restricts native static build settings. Metadata is not build provenance or semantic mapping proof.
Serialized fresh backend observation must agree with retained digest, positive PID and native architecture. Failure, cancellation or concurrent retirement refuses and permanently retires appraisal.

Both locally approved policy artifact and component descriptors must contain the exact image digest and verified owned bytes before fresh observation. This appraises a child, grants no admission, and cannot measure a parent calculator or implement parent-hop policy.
Appraisal retires before serialized child cleanup. Failed or cancelled cleanup retains backend ownership for retry; retire native work and preserve uncertain effect completions before termination.

Same memfd is written, made executable, sealed and rehashed before descriptor-based exec with empty environment and mandatory pidfd. Child wait and failed startup cleanup retain ownership; no mutable-path or PID-only fallback. Constants, descriptor assignments and comparison conditions are reviewed source hashed here, not proven by call matching.
Zero-timeout poll on retained nonnegative pidfd rejects exited or signalled state. Process lifetime is not a logical worker or exec generation.

Live proc executable must match retained device/inode/size/seals and bounded content hash. Bounded proc maps reject writable or foreign executable mappings; liveness is checked again. Not instruction-page attestation, atomic admission or exclusion of transient changes.
Terminates only the retained owned child through pidfd, waits for reap, then closes owned image and pidfd. Cancellation leaves resources for retry; successful cleanup is not rollback proof.

Parses executable mapping permissions and device/inode, permits only the sealed object plus named zero-inode kernel mappings, and requires an image mapping. Maps metadata does not inspect private instruction pages or prove complete isolation.
Unsupported platforms return ErrUnsupported without launching an executable or synthetic fallback. All build-tag variants are parsed, not executed by this query.
Harmless runtime fixture accepts only a literal calculate command and fixed addition. It has no native Guard/admission and remains an unmediated test fixture, not a protected production route.

limitations: Manual route classifications; AST matching does not prove authorization or reachability.
All tracked non-test Go files, including examples, generated code and all build tags, are parsed.
Selected route anchors are not an exhaustive effect graph; other declarations remain unclassified.
No type resolution, external dependencies, dynamically loaded plugins or reflective dispatch analysis.
Nested function calls belong to the enclosing declaration; package initializer calls are separate.
No ADK code, external LLM call, tool callback or deployment is executed by this query.
Native protection is opt-in and depends on isolated authoritative policy, registry, custody and loader bindings.
Exact-operation rules are trusted local root configuration; parent-hop policy is separate.
Factory.Load and Instance.Check remain trusted providers; snapshots and source queries do not attest actual loaded code.
Binding.Tool remains a trusted native configuration capability, not a model-facing unsigned dispatcher.
Artifact reading requires protected serialized administration; local gating does not establish OS isolation or durable distributed epochs.
Linux/macOS and unsupported-platform sources are both parsed; build-tag selection and execution are not observed.
The calculator adapter constructs a fixed statically compiled tool; it does not load code from snapshot artifacts.
Measurement.Check must establish protected verification before host image/dependency loading and retained immutable runtime identity; this query supplies no provider or deployment attestation.
The same private calculator callback is an opt-in trusted capability behind native admission; direct builtin and ordinary dispatch remain unmediated.
ADK unit and local runtime results with fixture Registry/measurement providers remain separate evidence; completed arithmetic can return a domain-error result.
The source set includes a harmless testdata host main; its RUNTIME_TEST_FIXTURE route has no native admission and is not a protected production route.
Sealed-image startup supports native Linux amd64/arm64 static Go executables only; all platform variants are parsed without executing them.
The caller must independently approve image bytes/digest and isolate administration, kernel/procfs, supervisor and host from untrusted writers; file seals are not a sandbox or isolation proof.
Executable backing-object identity and proc maps metadata are not live private instruction-page attestation, remote attestation or complete effect mediation.
Pidfd identifies process lifetime, not logical worker/exec generation; observations are not atomic with child admission and do not exclude transient changes.

Process.CheckSnapshot appraises the child executable and is not guardcalculator.Measurement for a parent calculator; protected child-to-supervisor binding and final native admission remain outstanding.
Sealed-image ADK unit and local/CI Linux runtime evidence is separate; this source query runs no ADK host and closes no deployed control or independent-hop gate.
